Subject: Re: QBR preflight: timeline gaps, mitigations & launch readiness

Status: at-risk
Biggest risk: Dedicated EU capacity is not validated for the expected peak QPS; current perf tests show tail latency spikes at projected load.
Proposed mitigation & owner:
- Short term (this week): enable extra reserved nodes in EU pool and reduce default batch size from 32->16 to lower tails (owner: infra/ops runbook by Marcus).
- Mid term: deploy kernel-level patch that reduces attention scratch allocation (target next week; owner: infra engineering — I will coordinate).
- Fallback: route EU traffic to hosted US cluster with data routing waiver for 48 hours if SLA breach imminent (requires approval).
Exec decision needed: yes — temporary capacity commit and potential cost delta.

Notes: I attached perf traces to the tracker and a link to the internal incident doc. If execs push back on committed reserve cost, we can propose a 72-hour cross-region failover with customer notice for minimal cost.

Marcus Lin
Director, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Status: delayed for two user-visible features (session-affinity and streaming-optimizations).
Biggest risk: Feature scope creep on the session-affinity work is blocking final e2e validation; the engineering estimate slipped by ~2 sprints due to an unanticipated dependency on our auth handshake flow.
Proposed mitigation & owner:
- Scope cut: deliver session affinity in a v1 with sticky tokens (no cross-region stickiness) to unblock the launch; postpone cross-region affinity to post-launch (owner: Laura + eng leads).
- Canary: ship streaming-optimizations to 10% of accounts behind a feature flag to validate perf before full rollout (owner: Product + Marcus for infra config).
Exec decision needed: no immediate budget ask, but would like approval to change planned GA feature set for the QBR messaging.

I added a short scope-cut doc to the tracker: feature-cut-scope.md — summarizes what's being delayed and why. This keeps us honest with customers and reduces delivery risk.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Dir, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Biggest risk: If we change the GA feature set and don't align on messaging, sales/CS will overpromise. We need a single public story for the QBR and a follow-up plan for the delayed items.
Proposed mitigation & owner:
- Messaging: draft public-facing bullet points that state "initial availability with core capabilities" and call out a roadmap for follow-ups (owner: Evelyn).
- CS prep: ask Monica in CS to prepare a short FAQ and a standard customer note for accounts on the MSA (owner: CS, looped after this thread).
- Exec ask: approval for the proposed scope cut messaging (yes/no).

Draft lines for the QBR slide (please react inline):
- "Launch readiness: Core inference capabilities ready for initial GA; selective advanced features deferred to H1 next year to ensure performance and reliability."
- "Mitigation: Canary releases and a staged roll-out limit customer impact while engineering completes cross-region affinity and streaming optimizations."

I can take the slide bullets and produce a one-pager for execs if you sign off on the messaging.

- Dec 10: EU reserved capacity increase in place
- Dec 17: Full GA launch (core)
- Jan 15: Post-GA cross-region session-affinity rollout
